reasons: The rule expects a transition-assistance and data-return clause; the only effect-of-termination provision (4(c)(i)-(iv)) covers cessation of services, licence revocation and a mutual 'return or destroy' election for Confidential Information, with no transition assistance, no data export in a usable format and no deletion certification — 'missing' is the correct classification and not double-flagged elsewhere.

The inserted 4(c)(v) tracks the playbook model language closely (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, deletion plus written certification) and is a targeted addition appended after 4(c)(iv) rather than a rewrite of existing text.
The precedence sentence over 4(c)(iv) is a necessary and minimal addition, since the existing destroy-at-election right would otherwise defeat the data-return obligation identified in the rationale.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required first-person plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change, and offers the 90-day fallback; deterministic checks corroborate that transition/data-return language is present in the redline.
